subject: Urban Planning
title: Islamabad: Pakistan's Planned Capital
description: A short lesson to help you apply Islamabad: Pakistan's Planned Capital.

hook.text: In 1960, Pakistan decided Karachi was too crowded and chaotic. A new capital was built from scratch.

buildup.text: Greek planner Constantinos Doxiadis designed Islamabad on a grid with numbered sectors and zones.

discovery.text: Each sector was self-contained with its own markets, mosques, and schools — a city of mini-cities.

twist.text: The plan ignored Rawalpindi next door. Two cities merged into one sprawling, unplanned metro area.

climax.text: Islamabad remains one of the greenest planned capitals, but its rigid grid frustrates residents.

punchline.text: A perfect grid on paper. A messy city in real life.

quiz.question: Who designed the plan for Islamabad?
